dedupe_keys.name: epa water treatment adsorption and ion exchange models

description: The US Environmental Protection Agency's water_treatment_models repository publishes contaminant-removal models for drinking-water treatment. It contains a pore/surface-diffusion adsorption model for granular activated carbon, an ion-exchange model and Shiny interfaces for granular carbon, ion exchange and powdered carbon. Python supplies the main numerical models, while R/Shiny provides selected interfaces. Users supply treatment-unit settings and contaminant properties or observations and obtain predicted treatment performance. Coverage is global and process-specific, not a fixed utility network or observation period. Public code and component documentation are free under MIT. A material limitation is the repository's explicit draft status: the code has not been reviewed or cleared by EPA. Users therefore cannot treat the repository as agency-endorsed design guidance or assume calibrated removal performance for untested contaminants. The tools can support treatment-process calibration and scenario comparisons within water-supply simulations, complementary to network-level EPANET modelling (model-epanet). The repository links the separate Environmental Technologies Design Option Tool but does not claim that the two are identical. No model input workbook or treatment dataset was downloaded.
